steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
You are the bioinformatician of a cancer-genomics core facility. Tumour and normal DNA of three
patients was sequenced on a small hybrid-capture panel. The clinical team needs, for every patient,
the tumour/normal pair and the somatic variants of the tumour.

Task directory:
- `/task`

Inputs (read-only) under `/task/input`:
- `fastq/<sample_id>_R1.fastq.gz`, `fastq/<sample_id>_R2.fastq.gz` - paired-end reads (2 x 100 nt),
  one pair of files per library (six libraries)
- `manifest.tsv` - sample sheet exported from the LIMS: `patient`, `sample_type` (`tumour` or
  `normal`), `sample_id`, `fastq_1`, `fastq_2`
- `reference/ref.fa` (+ `.fai`) - the panel reference, one contig (`chr22_panel`); no aligner index is
  provided
- `targets.bed` - the capture targets on the panel reference (0-based, half-open)
- `core_notes.md` - hand-over notes of the sequencing core

Available software (on `PATH`): `bwa`, `minimap2`, `samtools`, `bcftools` (with `bgzip`, `tabix`),
Python 3.12 with `pysam`, numpy, scipy and pandas. There is no internet access.

Your task:
1. Align the reads of every library to the panel reference.
2. Establish, for every patient, which normal library was prepared from the same individual as the
   patient's tumour library.
3. Call the somatic single-nucleotide variants and short insertions/deletions of every tumour
   inside the capture targets.

Required outputs under `/task/output`:
- `pairing.tsv` - tab-separated with the columns `patient`, `tumour_sample`, `normal_sample`; one
  row per patient of the manifest. `tumour_sample` is the `sample_id` of the patient's tumour
  library as listed in the manifest; `normal_sample` is the `sample_id` of the normal library that
  comes from the same individual as that tumour library.
- `somatic/<patient>.vcf.gz` - one gzip- or bgzip-compressed VCF per patient holding the somatic
  variants of that patient's tumour library.
  - A somatic variant is a single-nucleotide variant or short insertion/deletion that is present in
    tumour cells of the patient and absent from the patient's germline. Germline variants, and
    differences from the reference that arise during library preparation, sequencing or read
    alignment, are not somatic variants.
  - Reported variants have `FILTER` = `PASS`; records with any other FILTER value are not part of
    the deliverable.
  - `CHROM`, `POS`, `REF`, `ALT` follow the VCF specification relative to `reference/ref.fa`; one
    alternate allele per record; insertions and deletions left-aligned and parsimonious (the
    representation `bcftools norm` produces).
  - Every record carries `AF=<number>` in the `INFO` column: the fraction (0-1) of the tumour
    library's DNA fragments covering the site that carry the alternate allele.
  - The reporting range of the assay starts at an allele fraction of 5%; variants below it may be
    left out.
- `summary.json` - `{"patients": {"<patient>": {"tumour_sample": "<sample_id>", "normal_sample":
  "<sample_id>", "n_snv": <int>, "n_indel": <int>}, ...}}` where `n_snv` and `n_indel` are the
  numbers of `PASS` single-nucleotide and insertion/deletion records in that patient's VCF and the
  two sample ids repeat `pairing.tsv`.

Constraints:
- Do not modify anything under `/task/input`; write deliverables only under `/task/output`.
- Extra columns, INFO fields and sample columns are allowed.
- Do not ask for confirmation. Execute directly.

steps.message:
Analysis: There are six paired libraries (~23k–49k read pairs each), three manifest tumours, and three blood normals. The requested depth is realistic for the 46.3 kb panel. Since FASTQ sample IDs do not obviously guarantee correct tumour–normal pairing, correct normals must be inferred from genotype concordance. The panel is small, so BWA-MEM alignment, duplicate marking, and pileup-based pairwise comparison are practical.
Plan: Create an output-local working directory, build a BWA index there without touching the read-only reference directory, and align every library with proper read groups. Process each BAM through name sort, samtools fixmate, coordinate sort, duplicate marking, and indexing. Then print flagstats and on-target depth summaries to verify that all libraries align well and have adequate coverage.

arguments.keystrokes:
set -euo pipefail
REF=/task/input/reference/ref.fa
for s in CG24-4187 CG24-6425 CG24-7410 CG24-1366 CG24-9024 CG24-3973; do
  bwa mem -t 4 -R "@RG\tID:${s}\tSM:${s}\tPL:ILLUMINA\tLB:${s}" /task/output/work/ref.fa "/task/input/fastq/${s}_R1.fastq.gz" "/task/input/fastq/${s}_R2.fastq.gz" 2>"/task/output/work/${s}.bwa.log" \
    | samtools sort -n -@ 2 -o "/task/output/work/${s}.namesort.bam" -
  samtools fixmate -m -@ 2 "/task/output/work/${s}.namesort.bam" "/task/output/work/${s}.fixmate.bam"
  samtools sort -@ 2 -o "/task/output/work/${s}.sorted.bam" "/task/output/work/${s}.fixmate.bam"
  samtools markdup -@ 2 "/task/output/work/${s}.sorted.bam" "/task/output/work/${s}.bam"
  samtools index "/task/output/work/${s}.bam"
  rm -f "/task/output/work/${s}.namesort.bam" "/task/output/work/${s}.fixmate.bam" "/task/output/work/${s}.sorted.bam"
done

for s in CG24-4187 CG24-6425 CG24-7410 CG24-1366 CG24-9024 CG24-3973; do echo "=== $s ==="; samtools flagstat "/task/output/work/${s}.bam" | grep -E 'in total|properly paired|singletons|duplicates'; done

for s in CG24-4187 CG24-6425 CG24-7410 CG24-1366 CG24-9024 CG24-3973; do d=$(samtools depth -a -b /task/input/targets.bed "/task/output/work/${s}.bam" | awk '{s+=$3;n++} END{if(n)printf "%.2f",s/n; else print "0.00"}'); o=$(samtools view -c -L /task/input/targets.bed "/task/output/work/${s}.bam"); t=$(samtools view -c "/task/output/work/${s}.bam"); printf '%s\tmean_target_depth=%s\ton_target=%s/%s (%.1f%%)\n' "$s" "$d" "$o" "$t" "$(awk -v o=$o -v t=$t 'BEGIN{if(t)print 100*o/t; else print 0}')"; done

Analysis: All six BAMs are complete, 100% properly paired, about 97.5% on-target, and exceed the requested depth (tumours 175–188x, normals 87–95x). Alignment quality is therefore suitable. The next requirement is genotype-based identity matching of normals, followed by somatic calling.
Plan: Generate a high-quality joint multi-sample germline callset over the capture targets. Index and normalize it, then inspect genotype/allele-depth records. Pairwise concordance at informative germline sites will identify which blood library belongs to each tumour. Also summarize coverage by target to detect any problematic interval.
